1	# Working on archy
2	
3	Notes for a coding agent working *on* this repository. For using archy as a
4	tool, see [`skills/archy/SKILL.md`](skills/archy/SKILL.md) and the README.
5	
6	Everything here was learned by getting it wrong. Each rule names the failure it
7	came from, so you can judge whether it applies to what you are doing rather than
8	following it blindly.
9	
10	## Before you push: run what CI runs
11	
12	```bash
13	uv run ruff check          # NO path argument
14	uv run ruff format --check
15	uv run ty check
16	uv run pytest
17	uv run archy check .       # archy's own layer rules
18	uv run archy cycles . --strict
19	```
20	
21	**`ruff check` with no path.** Running `ruff check some/file.py` is not the same
22	command and will pass while CI fails: a fixture directory with deliberately
23	unused imports broke the build twice in one session because it was only ever
24	linted per-file.
25	
26	**The last two matter as much as the first four.** archy gates itself, so a new
27	fixture tree or bench sample can introduce a real cycle or layer violation in a
28	directory that is not archy's code. Add such trees to `exclude:` in `archy.yaml`
29	with the reason, rather than weakening a rule.
30	
31	**Open the failing check, never the tally.** A summary line saying "1 failed"
32	tells you nothing; `main` has been broken by merging on a green-looking count.
33	Fetch the job's failing *step*, then its log.
34	
35	## Adding a gate or a payload field
36	
37	**Wire it to every surface in one change.** At the time of writing there are
38	three, and check whether that is still current: the CLI's text output, the CLI's
39	`--format json`, and the MCP payload. A presence check shipped
40	to the CLI alone left the MCP surface, which is what agents actually call,
41	reporting `passed=true` for the exact case the check existed to catch. Three
42	consecutive review rounds each found one more surface it had been omitted from.
43	
44	**Test the serialized form, not the attribute.** FastMCP sends `model_dump()`,
45	which silently drops plain `@property`. A test asserting
46	`payload.coverage.layers_present == 0` passed while the wire format carried
47	nothing at all. Use `@computed_field` for derived values that consumers need,
48	and assert on `model_dump()`.
49	
50	**A verdict without a reason is not actionable.** `passed=false` with an empty
51	`violations` list is indistinguishable from a bug in archy. Whatever fails the
52	gate must also say why, in every format.
53	
54	## Review findings
55	
56	Reviews here regularly find real bugs, not just style. When a round finds
57	something substantive, run another round after fixing. `min_layers_present`
58	(#123, PR #371) needed four rounds, and rounds two, three and four each found a
59	distinct real defect: the gate missing from the MCP surface, the JSON output not
60	saying why it failed, and `model_dump()` dropping the reason entirely.
61	
62	**Pre-existing findings get filed, not folded in.** Widening a PR to fix code it
63	did not touch makes the diff harder to review and buries the actual change.
64	Precedent, all split out of unrelated PRs and all still readable as standalone
65	tickets: #317 (duplicated empty-package setup in the CLI tests), #318 (the
66	repeated Click bound-check validations), #335 (two duplicated text-renderer
67	blocks in `cli.py`). **Check for an existing ticket first** - it is easy to
68	file a duplicate of something a contributor is already working on.
69	
70	**Leave `good first issue` tickets alone.** Outside contributors pick these up;
71	several have landed. Filing new ones is welcome, taking them is not.
72	
73	## Measurement and benches
74	
75	Read [`docs/WHAT_DIDNT_WORK.md`](docs/WHAT_DIDNT_WORK.md) before proposing any
76	study. Three pre-registered claims have been measured and all three came back
77	null, and the write-up explains what that does and does not license.
78	
79	**Build and validate the measurement before spending agent time.** Live agent
80	runs are the only expensive part of any bench here. Every harness bug found
81	during a paid run is a run wasted, and the arm-B pilot found five plumbing bugs
82	that would each have cost the whole batch had they not been caught by a
83	one-task smoke run first.
84	
85	**Pre-register the thresholds, including the ones that kill your idea.** Write
86	them into the repository before running. `p_B <= 10%` and the four decay nulls
87	were committed in advance, which is the only reason reading them afterwards was
88	honest. **Do not reinterpret a threshold to keep a signal alive.**
89	
90	**Audit results for artifact-shaped numbers before believing them.** A metric
91	that is exactly `0.0000` for every repository, or an implausibly high count, is
92	an artifact until proven otherwise. The decay study carried six such artifacts,
93	and **every one of them biased toward the answer the study wanted**: it would
94	have reported 57% where the truth was 11%.
95	
96	**Unmeasurable runs are dropped, never scored clean.** Counting a run that could
97	not be analysed as a pass biases the rate by exactly the runs that broke.
98	
99	## Config and rules
100	
101	**A rule set that cannot fire looks exactly like a clean codebase.** Two shipped
102	bench configs had patterns matching one empty `__init__.py` instead of a
103	338-module package, so every rule in them was dead and `check` exited 0. Layer
104	patterns are `pkg.**`, not `pkg`, which matches an exact dotted name.
105	
106	Whenever you author rules for a codebase, **canary them**: add one deliberately
107	violating import, confirm exit 1, revert. `bench/q1b_layers_check.py --canary`
108	does this for the bench configs.
109	
110	## Git and GitHub
111	
112	- Branch and open a PR. Never push to `main`.
113	- Use `gh api` REST. `gh pr edit` and `--json` flags go through GraphQL, which
114	  can fail while still exiting 0.
115	- Merging a stacked PR with `--delete-branch` auto-closes its child, and a
116	  closed PR's base cannot be retargeted.
